step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates ZS Associates' self-service enterprise data engineering platform built on AWS. 1. Users (data engineers/analysts) log into a web portal running on EC2 instances to request infrastructure provisioning or data access. 2. The portal submits request metadata to core microservices running on an Amazon EKS cluster. 3. EKS logs request details into an Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL) database. 4. EKS pushes workflow messages to an Amazon SQS queue. 5. EKS worker pods consume messages from SQS to execute infrastructure automation. 6. EKS provisions resources across IAM (and Apache Ranger policies), Amazon EMR clusters, AWS Glue Data Catalog, target provisioned EC2 instances (running containerized Airflow/NiFi), and Amazon S3 buckets. 7. EKS triggers Amazon SES to notify users upon workflow completion. 8. S3 datasets are cataloged into Glue Data Catalog via crawlers and exposed back through EKS microservices to the portal for self-service data discovery.

nodes.name: USERS
nodes.notes: Data engineers, analysts, and data scientists interacting with the self-service portal.

nodes.name: EC2 (Portal)
nodes.notes: Hosts the web interface for selecting pipeline types and entering chargeback codes.

nodes.name: EKS
nodes.notes: Central Amazon EKS cluster running 100+ microservices, crawlers, and automation workers.

nodes.name: POSTGRESQL
nodes.notes: Stores request records, metadata, and status logs.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Holds infrastructure provisioning and data access workflow event messages.

nodes.name: SES
nodes.notes: Sends approval requests and status notifications to data owners and requesters.

nodes.name: IAM
nodes.notes: Manages AWS identity policies integrated with Apache Ranger for fine-grained access control.

nodes.name: EMR
nodes.notes: Provisioned EMR clusters for batch big data processing.

nodes.name: GLUE CATALOG
nodes.notes: Stores metadata databases, schemas, and dataset access definitions.

nodes.name: EC2 (Provisioned)
nodes.notes: Target compute provisioned with containerized Apache Airflow or NiFi for data pipelines.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Enterprise data lake storage buckets containing raw and processed datasets.

edges.notes: User submits infrastructure or data access request via web portal.
Portal forwards request details to EKS microservices.
EKS logs request metadata record into PostgreSQL.
EKS publishes workflow event message to SQS queue.
EKS automation worker picks up workflow execution message from SQS.
EKS configures IAM roles and updates Apache Ranger access policies.
EKS provisions Amazon EMR cluster for batch analytics.
EKS registers databases and schema definitions in Glue Catalog.
EKS provisions EC2 instance running Airflow or NiFi.
EKS provisions Amazon S3 buckets for project storage.
EKS triggers SES notification upon successful provisioning.
SES delivers resource access details and confirmation email to user.
S3 dataset changes are cataloged by Glue crawlers.
EKS metadata service queries Glue Catalog to expose data discovery dashboard in portal.
